style file: pure-function unit test layout in this package

acceptance: normalize sorts, clamps and drops empty or style-less ranges: given unsorted ranges including one with start >= end, one with no colour and one ending past a text length of 10, expect sorted ranges clamped to 10 with the empty and style-less ones gone
normalize merges adjacent ranges with identical style and resolves overlaps: given [0,3) red, [3,5) red, and [4,8) highlight yellow, expect [0,4) red, [4,5) red + yellow, [5,8) yellow
applyTextStyle splits a range and keeps the other property: given [0,10) color red + highlight yellow, apply { color: blue } to [3,6), expect [0,3) red+yellow, [3,6) blue+yellow, [6,10) red+yellow

applyTextStyle with null removes only that property: given [0,10) red + yellow, apply { highlight: null } to [2,4) and separately { color: null } to [0,10), expect the highlight is gone only on [2,4); the second call leaves only the yellow highlight
applyTextStyle fills uncovered gaps: given no ranges, apply { highlight: yellow } to [2,5) of a length-8 text, expect [{ start: 2, end: 5, highlight: yellow }] with no color key

diffText derives a single replacement: given pairs: identical strings; insertion in the middle; deletion at the end; replacement of a repeated character, expect null; { from, to: from, insertLength }; { from, to, insertLength: 0 }; a minimal edit that never has to < from
shiftStyleRanges moves ranges after an insertion and keeps those before: given [0,2) and [5,8), insert 3 characters at 3, expect [0,2) and [8,11)
insertion strictly inside a range extends it, at a boundary it does not: given [2,5), insert 1 character at 3, then separately at 2 and at 5, expect [2,6); [3,6); [2,5)
deletion shrinks overlapping ranges and drops emptied ones: given [2,6) and [7,9), delete [4,8), expect [2,4) and [4,5)

getStyledLines maps ranges across a soft wrap that dropped whitespace: given originalText "hello world", text "hello\nworld", range [4,7) red, expect line 0 runs "hell" plain and "o" red; line 1 runs "w" red and "orld" plain

getStyledLines maps ranges across hard newlines and kept whitespace: given originalText "ab
cd ef", text "ab
cd 
ef", range [1,7) highlight yellow, expect runs carry yellow on "b", "cd " and "e" with correct start offsets
getStyledLines with no ranges returns one plain run per non-empty line: given text with an empty middle line, expect [[run], [], [run]] with color and highlight null
getStyledRunPositions honours alignment and RTL: given widths [10, 20] in a box of width 100 for left, center, right and right+rtl, expect [0,10], [35,45], [70,80], [90,70]
getUniformRangeStyle reports a shared value only: given [0,4) red and [4,8) blue, expect red for [1,3); null for [2,6); null for a gap

sanitizeStyleRanges drops malformed entries: given a string; and an array with non-integer offsets, a numeric colour, an entry with no colour and an out-of-bound end, expect null; only valid entries, clamped and normalised

picking the element's stroke colour clears a range's text colour: given a red range then the same selection picked with the element strokeColor, expect no styleRanges entry carries a color

a bound label's highlight does not change its container: given a rectangle with a bound text, editing the label with a sub-range selected, background pick, expect the label has the highlight range and the rectangle backgroundColor is unchanged
typing before a range shifts it: given range [12,19) then the value changed to "A Bid request timeout", expect the range becomes [14,21)
with no selection the stroke pick changes strokeColor: given editing with a collapsed caret, stroke pick red, expect strokeColor is red and styleRanges is absent
undo restores the previous ranges and redo re-applies them: given a range pick, then exit the editor, undo, redo, expect after undo no range carries the picked colour; after redo the range is back

paste styles does not copy ranges: given a styled text A and a plain text B, copy styles from A (actionCopyStyles) and paste onto B (actionPasteStyles), expect B has no styleRanges and A keeps its own
